Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. # - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.

payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is there reliable visual evidence that the source mug has undergone a relevant change toward being moved to the right of the headphones, without requiring proof that the requested placement is complete?
node.criteria: Pass only when visual evidence reliably establishes a relevant change to the source mug or its placement toward the requested move, even if the final right-of-headphones placement is not established. Fail only when visual evidence reliably establishes that the source mug remains unchanged and no relevant progress toward the requested move occurred. Use unknown when the evidence cannot reliably establish either relevant progress or its absence. Do not count a blurred remnant, a mug-shaped object at the destination, color similarity, or position alone as progress unless its shape, appearance, and relation to the source scene reliably connect it to a relevant change of the source mug. Keep this progress judgment distinct from whether the source mug is confirmed to be right of the headphones.
node.binding: Compare the source image's large light-blue mug, including its body and handle, with the edited scene. Inspect the former location and any candidate mugs for reliable evidence of a relevant change to the source mug or its placement; allow for changes in appearance, scale, and lighting, but do not infer source identity from color or position alone. A pass means relevant progress toward the requested move is established, not that the requested placement is fulfilled.

node_traces.evidence: The source has one large light-blue mug left of the headphones. In the edited image, a blurred blue remnant remains near the former location, while two smaller, differently rendered mugs appear elsewhere, including one to the right of the headphones. The remnant and candidate mugs do not reliably establish that the source mug itself was moved or otherwise changed toward the requested placement; their appearance and relation to the source mug are ambiguous.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s conservative identity rule is appropriate, but it appears overconstrained for this case: the edited image shows a strong blurred blue remnant at the mug’s former location and a mug-shaped object to the right of the headphones, while the original large blue mug is absent as a clearly intact object. Together these are evidence of a likely attempted move with incomplete/uncertain execution, not proof of no progress; the trace currently collapses that evidence to unknown. Refine the binding/criteria to assess the scene-level transformation jointly (former-location remnant, destination candidate, and source-object disappearance/continuity), allowing a partial-progress judgment when these cues coherently support an attempted relocation even if identity or final placement is not certain. Keep unknown for genuinely inconclusive or conflicting cues, and do not treat a destination mug or color/position alone as sufficient. The high-confidence unknown merits review of the evidence-to-status calibration, not simply lowering confidence or forcing the reference label. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated."}
